methodology_note:
Public sources provide useful benchmarks but do not establish a universal mover-price coefficient. U-Haul states that one-way prices vary by origin, destination, truck size, move date 
and inventory. The calculator therefore uses the mileage-band average only as a lower bound on the DIY 
base cost, so no estimate falls below the average one-way truck rental for its distance band; it is not 
used as a per-mile coefficient, a quote or a guaranteed rate. BLS and Census figures remain context 
only.

uhaul.name: U-Haul, How To Save Money On Truck Rentals
uhaul.use: one-way truck rental market benchmark by mileage band

bls.name: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, Occupational Employment and Wages, May 2025
bls.use: labor-cost benchmark only; not a mover quote

census.name: U.S. Census Bureau, ACS 1-year State-to-State Migration Flows, 2024
census.use: route-demand/context signal; not a price coefficient

uhaul.documented_rule:
One-way rates depend on origin, destination, truck size, move date and rental 
truck inventory.

candidate_coefficients.reason:
Do not convert the U-Haul distance-band averages, BLS labor wage, or Census migration 
flows into universal coefficients without route, truck-size, labor-scope and date calibration. The 
current planning model remains explicit until that calibration is supported by enough observations.
